lines.text: But dearest—Did you not understand that I understood?
lines.note: Early exchange showing she had already understood his words.

lines.text: This time, they brought me your letter at six o’clock yesterday evening: was I startled, or no, do you think, as I received it?
lines.note: His first startle at receiving her letter and relief that all proved kind.

lines.text: Now I will kiss you, dearest: used you to divine that at the very beginning, I have sometimes shortened the visit in order to arrive at the time of taking your hand?
lines.note: Private habit of shortening visits to reach the moment of taking her hand.

lines.text: I have just come from the vestry of Paddington chapel, and bore it very well, and saw nobody except one woman.
lines.note: Her small victory of bearing the vestry and seeing almost no one.

lines.text: I wonder what I shall write to you, Ba—I could suppress my feelings here, as I do on other points, and say nothing of the hatefulness of this state of things which is prolonged so uselessly.
lines.note: His confession of the hatefulness of their prolonged separation.

lines.text: Let me get the kiss I lost on Saturday! (I dined at Arnould’s yesterday with Chorley and his brother, and the Cushmans.)
lines.note: Callback to the kiss lost on Saturday after dining with Chorley and the Cushmans.

lines.text: Only a few words to tell you that Flush is found, and lying on the sofa, with one paw and both ears hanging over the edge of it.
lines.note: Flush found at last, lying on the sofa with one paw hanging over.

lines.text: The sight of your letter, even, did not provoke the cloud—that was only the lesser joy, I thought, preceding the greater!
lines.note: Her smile at his phrase about the grave man and woman talking business.

lines.text: I am delighted to know Flush is with you, if I am not.
lines.note: His rejoicing that Flush is with her even if he is not.

lines.text: How unwell you are, dearest beloved!
lines.note: Her alarm at how unwell he is and wish for the exact truth.

lines.text: Ever dearest, I write a word that you may read it and know how all is safe so far, and that I am not slain downright with the day—oh, such a day!
lines.note: Her word after the wedding day, still not slain by it.

lines.text: Ah—I shall not be first to leave off that—see if I shall!
lines.note: Her promise not to be first to stop openly loving him.

lines.text: You take my words from me—I ‘exult’ in the irrevocability of this precious bestowal of yourself on me—come what will my life has borne flower and fruit—it is a glorious, successful, felicitous life, I thank God and you.
lines.note: His exultation in the irrevocability of her bestowal of herself.

lines.text: By to-morrow at this time, I shall have you only, to love me—my beloved!
lines.note: Her farewell certainty that by tomorrow she will have him only.
